lead: Savannah plumbing deals with heat, humidity, tidal flooding, hurricanes and some of the oldest homes in Georgia. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Savannah.
risk: old cast-iron and galvanized pipes, flood backups and storm damage
why: The Historic District and the Victorian District have homes from the 1800s with galvanized supply lines, cast-iron drains and old sewer laterals. Many sit on raised foundations with exposed pipes.
Heavy rain, king tides and hurricanes flood low streets and back up drains. Rare hard freezes burst pipes under raised homes.
water: Savannah pumps water from the Upper Floridan Aquifer and treats surface water from Abercorn Creek. It is moderately hard.
tips: Check historic district rules before exterior work.
Shut off the main valve before a hurricane evacuation.
Wrap exposed pipes before a freeze.
Scope the sewer line before buying an older home.
areas: PipeMend works in the Historic District, the Victorian District, Ardsley Park, Midtown, the Southside, Isle of Hope and every other Savannah neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Savannah Development Services, and plumbers must be licensed by the Georgia State Division of Master and Journeyman Plumbers.

faq.q: Are there special plumbing rules in Savannah's Historic District?
faq.a: Work that changes a building's outside, such as new vents or exterior lines, may need historic review. Interior plumbing usually needs only a regular permit.
